subject: physics
question_text: What is latent heat of vaporization?

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2025 (Q8) — Section A, 2 marks. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced from that paper. Physics hand-checked: the latent heat of vaporization is the heat needed to convert unit mass of a liquid into vapour at its boiling point with no change of temperature, Q = mL, unit J kg⁻¹; for water L = 22.6 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ at 100 °C (NCERT Class-11 value).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The latent heat of vaporization is the
heat needed to change one kilogram of a
liquid into vapour at its boiling point,
steps.margin_note: First mark. Unit mass and no temperature change must both appear.
steps.why: While a liquid boils the supplied energy goes into separating its molecules, not into raising their speed, so the thermometer stays at the boiling point throughout.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the words unit mass. Latent heat is defined for one kilogram, not for the whole sample.

recall.must_convey: That it is the heat needed to change unit mass of a liquid into vapour at its boiling point without a change of temperature.

steps.memory_tip: Latent means hidden: the heat is supplied but the temperature does not change.

steps.label: The formula and its unit

lines.text: Q = mL,  L in J kg⁻¹

lines: L is the latent heat of vaporization of
the liquid and m is the mass vaporized.
For water L = 22.6 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹ at 100 °C.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The formula Q = mL together with the unit J kg⁻¹.
steps.why: The energy needed is proportional to the mass being vaporized, so the total heat is the mass multiplied by the heat needed for one kilogram.
common_mistakes: Giving the unit of L as joule. It is joule per kilogram, J kg⁻¹.

recall.must_convey: That Q = mL and the unit of L is J kg⁻¹.

steps.memory_tip: Multiply by the mass: Q = mL, where L is the heat for one kilogram.

insider_note: Two marks — the definition carrying unit mass and no change of temperature, then Q = mL with the unit J kg⁻¹.
